subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw keep Docker `no-new-privileges` mandatory for sandbox containers, add an explicit dangerous opt-out, or limit the fix to diagnostics/image compatibility for affected hosts?
rationale: The user-visible failure is real, but the narrow recovery path changes the Docker sandbox security boundary or adds a new config surface, which repository policy treats as maintainer-owned product/security direction.

options.title: Add audited opt-out
options.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` enabled by default, add a clearly named dangerous opt-out with doctor/security reporting, and require real Docker proof on an affected host.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Leave the hardening mandatory and add doctor/status/session diagnostics that explain the host incompatibility and point users to supported host/runtime fixes.

options.title: Investigate image/runtime fix first
options.body: Hold config changes until maintainers can prove whether the default sandbox image or host Docker/runc/AppArmor combination can be made compatible without weakening the flag.

recommendation.title: Add audited opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` enabled by default, add a clearly named dangerous opt-out with doctor/security reporting, and require real Docker proof on an affected host.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is centered on sandbox security/config policy, and recent history shows this owner repeatedly touching those exact surfaces.
